articleTitle: Applications of Picture Memories in Television Receivers
abstract: Digital serial CCD memory chips with a capacity of 308 Kbit allow to build picture memories with just a small number of packages and few control signals, as the device has inherent addressing.

articleTitle: A Digital Field Memory for Television Receivers
abstract: In this paper a description and a specification are presented of a 308 kbit digital field memory chip. This device, which is manufactured in a 2 um NMOS process and operates up to 40 MHz, has been designed especially for video applications. Aspects of the design are highlighted with respect to the application in television receivers.

articleTitle: A Proposal for Standardization of Home Bus System for Home Automation
abstract: In order to combine home electronic and electrical equipment effectively and realize Home Automation (HA), it is essential to establish a standard for information distribution newtowks and interfaces which can be used for those equipment. In this paper we propose a plan for standardization of the Home Bus System (HBS). This plan has been created after a number of experiments for various applications have been conducted toward HA for two years.

articleTitle: Novel Technologies for Automatic Focusing and White Balancing of Solid State Color Video Camera
abstract: The consumer video market is rapidly spreading. In response, development of color video camera is strongly accelerated in these several years.

articleTitle: Field Integration Mode CCD Color Television Camera using a Frequency Interleaving Method
abstract: A field integration mode CCD color television camera using a frequency interleaving method has been developed. Excellent picture quality without field time lag and aliasing was obtained. A small size, light weight and low power consumption color video camera with an all IC electronic circuit has been developed.

articleTitle: A Rotary Head High Density Digital Audio Tape Recorder
abstract: An exclusive rotary head type digital audio recorder (DAT) for consumer use has been developed. Guard-bandless azimuth digital recording method used in the captioned recorder has achieved the world's highest area recording density of 120 MBPI2 (λ=0.66μ, T.P= llμ). As a result, the experiment system enables recording of 2 CH 16-bit PCM signal at 44.1 kHz sampling frequency at a tape speed of 6 mm/s, using a 3.81 mm wide tape. The size of the cassette has been reduced to half the size of compact cassettes, while enabling three hours of continucus reccrding/playback. Simultaneously, the small drum (ϕ30) and 90°wrap mechanism have realized quick access at 200 times normal speed and simplified compact-size.

articleTitle: Ghost Clean System
abstract: The ghost is one of the most serious problems in TV reception. A variety of approaches have been tried to obtain a ghost-free TV picture, since the early days of TV broadcasting. Among them, a transversal filter type ghost canceller has been enthusiastically studied during the last decade.

articleTitle: Feature IC'S for Digivision TV Sets
Practical Considerations in the Design of Horizontal Deflection Systems for High-Definition Television Displays
abstract: In recent years, the quality of the picture displayed by commercial television receivers has been improved to the extent that further improvement is difficult to achieve within the framework of existing display techniques. Additional improvement could be obtained through improvements in color picture tubes, better signal processing, and through modification of current NTSC standards. However, modification of NTSC standards may not be acceptable unless the changes are compatible with the circuitry in the receivers already installed in millions of homes and do not make these receivers obsolete. Alternate approaches are being explored that do not require a change in transmission standards, but provide an improvement in observed picture quality through the elimination of certain artifacts in the picture.

articleTitle: Integrated Feature TV Concept with Serial I2C-Bus-Control and Field Memory
Practical TV Ghost Canceller using 2-Stage CCD Transversal Filter
abstract: On account of increasing skyscrapers in the urban area, TV ghost interference has become a serious problem and ghost cancellation is regarded as an indispensable item to improve TV broadcasting reception.

articleTitle: A Digital CTV Chassis Concept
Monolithic Filter and its Application to TV MPX Sound Decoder IC
abstract: In addition to giving the best possible picture and sound quality, today's color TV set is also required to absorb all of the reception expansions, such as sound multiplex, teletext, be able to be interfaced with video recorders and videotex, etc. The color TV is expected to do all this without a great increase in cost, and, of course, at a low failure level. The fundamental parts of the color TV system need to be standardized. If the signal processing parts were standardized, dimensions and power consumption decreased, these parts could be used in all sets, even pocket-sized televisions, and the number of engineers working on these fundamental systems could be reduced.

articleTitle: Constant Luminance Video Recording and Direct Satellite Broadcasting
abstract: In the last few years a spate of publications has appeared regarding extended and high-definition colour television systems expressing the need for more lines and fields/second and for a reduction in flicker, crossluminance and cross-colour effects. Digital and analogue recording of the three component signals Y, R-Y and B-Y, and the transmission of the analogue component signals by time-division multiplex have all received consideration.

articleTitle: New Polyphonic Sound Generator Chip with Integrated Microprocessor-Programmable ADSR Envelope Shaper
abstract: This paper proposes a new polyphonic sound generator LSI IC. The main features of the device are described, including eighth-order polyphonicity, integration of software-programmable ADSR envelope generators and direct microcomputer interfacing. By means of the presented IC, a wide range of polyphonic instruments can be easily synthesized. Finally, different system configurations are presented.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Design of Color Picture Tubes with a Three-Dimensional Model
abstract: Many cathode ray tubes for color television now incorporate non-cylindrical electrodes. The tapered rectangular slot in the beam-forming region [1] , and the overlapping lens [2] for the three beams are typical. The new computer model described here enables the engineer to compare the effects of varied electrode shapes without the expense of building an actual gun. Existing axisymmetric models [3-8] are of only limited use, since an accurate simulation requires the fully three dimensional model to treat angularly varying applied fields and space-charge fields. Here the entire tube is modelled from the cathode to the screen in two or three sections. Experimental and computed spot sizes are in excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Modular Video IF Concept
abstract: We have developed a new family of monolithic wide-band video IF-amplifiers, based on a modular design concept. This allows both short realisation times for different requirements and optimal chip sizes. The pinning provides optimal decoupling and permits the use of one print layout for the whole family.

articleTitle: A Single Chip PLL IC with a 150 MHz Dual Modulus Prescaler
abstract: Frequency synthesizers have been introduced into many TV sets due to the advantages of direct channel selection and the stability of the tuner oscillator.

articleTitle: Four Standard Colour Decoder with Picture Improvement
Harmonic Analysis of a Planar-Wound Toroidal Deflection Coil
abstract: We present analytical calculations to demonstrate how the mechanical constraints of the winding process limit the harmonic content of a planar-wound toroidal deflection coil and how one can change the various harmonics beyond this limitation by adding auxiliary turns to the coil. The results would be useful in application of theoretical knowledge about harmonics to the design of magnetic deflection coils.

articleTitle: Digital Audio Modulation in the PAL and NTSC Laservision Video Disc Coding Formats
abstract: We present an extension of the current LaserVision video disc format that includes a digital audio signal. We show the feasibility of a combined digital audio signal according to the Compact Disc Digital Audio format and the current analog audio signals in the NTSC video format, enabling the realization of a compatible system. For the PAL and SECAM video formats we show the feasibility of digital audio, but unfortunately it cannot be combined with the analog audio carriers.

articleTitle: High Quality, Electron Beam Sound Recording on Film
abstract: In the project of developing a method of transferring pictures from the high definition video system (HDVS) to 35mm motion picture film, a new audio recording method was sought which would match the quality of HDVS. This objective was achieved with a new system that produces a stereo sound track of the variable area type directly on the film by an electron beam.

articleTitle: High Performance Dual Dolby B-Tyre Noise Reduction IC for Low Voltage Applications
abstract: Recent advances in tape transport mechanism, tape head, and headset design have led to significant fidelity improvements of personal portable stereo playback and record/play systems using only two 1.5V battery cells.

articleTitle: Low Power Consumption Solid State Humidity Sensor
abstract: As controlling of comfortable environments and economical energy for consumer and industrial use, high reliability humidity sensors have been in widespread demand for sometime in applications such as air conditioning devices.

articleTitle: An Automatic Hue and Differential Phase Correction Scheme for NTSC Receivers Using A New Vertical Interval Reference Signal
abstract: The phase errors between the regenerated subcarrier and chrominance signal results in wrong reproduction of hue in a NTSC receiver and requires frequent adjustment of the hue control. The VIR system which was developed to perform automatic hue control in NTSC receivers eliminates only static phase errors but does not correct differential phase. This paper proposes a modified Vertical Interval Reference signal for automatic correction of hue and differential phase errors in NTSC system, and describes the design and development of associated receiver circuitry. Experimental results based on simulatued errors are presented.

articleTitle: New LSI I.C. Leads the Way to 5V TV Sets
abstract: Two among many objectives that influ-ence most of TV manufacturer choices are going to become the first in order of priority, they are: 1) utilization of very sophisticated multifunction IC in order to reduce to minimum calibrations, external components and assembling complexity 2) Reduction of total power consumption

articleTitle: Stereo Audio on CED Videodiscs
abstract: We have described the important elements of the CED VideoDisc stereo system. Experience with recording and testing early stereo programs for the catalog has confirmed (in the authors' opinion) that concerts and many feature films are significantly enhanced with this new CED VideoDisc stereo system.

articleTitle: New Motor Control Methods for Home VCR
abstract: The development of a new method of driving the brushless DC motor, called the QUASI-SINE WAVE method, reduces motor torque ripple to one quarter that of the conventional method. New methods for controlling the noiseless still and slow modes have also been developed; the former being to drive the capstan motor corresponding to the time interval between the noise band position and the head switching signal, while the latter controls the capstan motor in the drive-coast-damp mode, and takes care of stop control. The circuits required for these methods have been incorporated in three IC's.

articleTitle: Audio Noise Reduction IC with New Signal Processing
abstract: An audio noise reduction IC which includes all the necessary functions of the Dolby B and C type noise reduction systems has been developed by applying new signal processing. The new signal processing has made the circuit configuration simple and the application versatile with improving tne performance.

articleTitle: Application of Microcomputer-Based Control System to Instantaneous Gas Water Heater
abstract: There is an increasing demand for high quality hot water supply equipment which will provide hot water at the exact desired temperature, save energy, save space, and which has easy operation.

articleTitle: A Multifunction Home Control System
abstract: A multifunction Home Control System is described, which combines HVAC, security alarm, hazard alarm, emergency alarm, lighting and appliance control into one central system. A unique "touch bar" concept is used to simplify the control panel, and provision is made for the easy addition of other features and functions to installed systems.

articleTitle: Lucy/Lucinda--A Fully Integrated Solution to Videotex Terminal Interfaces
abstract: This paper describes how switched-capacitor techniques can be employed to achieve the monolithic integration of all the analogue circuitry required in a Videotex MODEM. The application of these techniques leads to a low cost fully integrated solution to the Videotex MODEM suitable for use in both Videotex terminals and home computers.

articleTitle: New Approaches to Low Cost Electronic Circuit Packages
abstract: The electronics industry has affected the American culture more profoundly than any other industry in our better than two hundred years as a nation. Television has significantly impacted our nation's habits for the past thirty to forty years. The method employed in design and manufacture of these consumer electronic products has evolved through three phases. Initially, consumer electronic circuits employed vacuum tubes as the major building block. Associated with the tube was a quick disconnect or tube socket and related terminal strip used as an interconnect and mounting system for passive components associated with the tube socket. These circuits were normally hand wired and hand soldered, although there were some attempts to automate the assembly operation thru the use of wire wrap terminals or solder cups. It was not until semiconductor devices came into wide usage and the printed circuit board replaced the terminal strip and tube socket, the door opened for automation. Approximately 1960, automatic assembly of printed circuit boards was employed by some of the larger electronic manufacturers. Most passive components employed in these circuits were substantially unchanged from the earlier vacuum tube circuits. Additionally, components could only be mounted on one side of the circuit board. The third phase is "surface mount" assembly whereby both sides of the printed circuit board is utilized. Cost and quality benefits along with accompanying size reduction will cause "surface mount" assembly systems to become the dominant circuit packaging method employed in consumer electronic packages as we move into the 1980's.

articleTitle: Recording Video Camera in the Beta Format
abstract: In this paper we shall introduce the small diameter head drum VCR System that uses exactly the same recording format as the original large diameter head drum system. Having identified the different factors of the tape pattern with the mechanical parts, we were able to develop a new technique of recording the same information as is done in the original format. As this is specialized for only recording, we were able to drastically reduce the number of both the mechanical parts and circuits in our compact all-in-one camera/VCR.

articleTitle: C-MAC--A High Quality Television Service for DBS
Television Receiver using a Pure Synchronous Detector IC
abstract: This paper describes a new excellent video detector IC for color television receivers with phase lock loop ( PLL ) operating at the intermediate frequency of 58.75 MHz generator. The IC includes IF amplifier, AGC circuit, VCO, video processing circuit, video detector, automatic phase control ( APC ) circuit, lock-unlock condition detector and AFC circuit. Using this system, better performance than a traditional diode detector or a quasi synchronous detector has been achieved with no increase of manufacturing cost.

articleTitle: Video Recording and Playback Systems--Beta Hi-Fi VCR
abstract: There has been a rapid penetration rate of home VCRs throughout the world. Technological advancements have brought forth a variety of multi-featured, compact, long-recording time models. High density recording has become the answer to the demand for high performance, and high quality products. However, in order to achieve this, the tape speed was lowered. The conventional fixed head bias recording system caused a deterioration in the audio playback frequency response characteristics, an increase in wow and flutter, etc., which all resulted in poor sound quality.

articleTitle: An Approach to Character Generation using Cubic Splines
abstract: The importance of Computer Graphics as a medium of man-machine communication cannot be over- emphasized. Until recently, computer graphics technology was relatively expensive to permit its widespread use. However, with the rapid decline in the cost of LSI hardware and display devices, computer graphics has found acceptance in diverse applications such as Computer Aided Design, real- time simulation, video displays, animation and home computers.

articleTitle: Single Chip IC with Head Drivers and Pre-Amplifiers for Home VCR
abstract: The first designing has been made of a fully integrated home VCR IC including head drive amplifiers, Pre-amplifiers and Rec/PB peripheral switches. In order to obtain a good C/N ratio (Carrier to Noise ratio), pre-amp design was optimized by CAD simulation with head and rotary transformer equivalent circuits derived from S parameters measured with a network analyzer. An obtained high C/N ratio of 57.5dB at 4MHz is excellent in comparison to those of conventional discrete transistors. The head drive amplifiers were designed in consideration of reducing power consumption. Head peripheral switches are completely incorporated into one chip with drive amps and pre-amps. Thus the peripheral components number was reduced by 1/2 and the power consumption was reduced to 1/2~1/5 compared with conventional types.

articleTitle: New Systems for Video Processing ICs
abstract: In improving the playback picture quality of a VCR, working particularly on improving the reduction of the crosstalk of the chroma signal from the neighboring tracks, and the signal to noise ratio, we concentrated on a modified feedback combfilter, in making up the complex combfilter system. Also, we were able to construct a nearly ideal VCO (Voltage Controlled Oscillator) System used in a color-APC (Automatic Phase Control). Its oscillation frequency is quite stable and it has a wide controllable frequency range. In these two systems we used a comparatively large value capacitor that makes it possible to achieve their special characteristics. Making use of the small elements including the large value capacitance found in the fine IC-process, we were able to fit these systems onto several ICs.

articleTitle: A Speech Synthesis Device using Formant and Residual Information
abstract: A new speech synthesis device has been developed. This speech synthesizer is based on a formant synthesizer and uses residual information. Generally, synthesized speech using residual information has high quality. In this speech synthesizer, the residual information is introduced as FIR (Finite Impulse Response) filter coefficients. Great flexibility in bit rate can be obtained by this implementation. Speech synthesis experiment showed the flexibility and the high performance for this speech synthesizer. This speech synthesizer can be applied to a high quality text to speech synthesis system and many other systems.

articleTitle: A New Self-Alignment System for Television Receivers in LSI Era
abstract: Since about 1972, the development and introduction of ICs has progressed, in order to improve the performance of TV receivers, with fairly satisfactory results. At present, technology has progressed to the point where two ICs upon which the equivalent of about 1000 elements has been integrated are used to form a small-signal system, but now simple accumulation of various IC's functions on one chip no longer results in significant improvements.

articleTitle: Deflection-Yoke Design for the Coty-29 Color-Picture Tube Display System
Problems of Ganging LC and RC Tuned Circuits Together
abstract: Ganging LC and RC tuned circuits is investigated. Formulae determining ganging errors are derived (a case of two zero error points is considered). Broadcasting receivers are taken into account as a subject of potential applications. Calculations of ganging errors which would appear in radio broadcasting bands are presented. A possibility of using RC heterodyne oscillators in LC tuned broadcasting receivers is discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetic Circuit of Flyback Transformers and Relevant Measurements
abstract: The magnetic circuit of flyback transformers of television receivers is analyzed. Formulas for the number of turns of primary coil and the thickness of the air gap are derived. Then the requirements on the U-cores are discussed. Various measurements may be made with a simple line output circuit. The waveform of the current in the primary coil may be observed and equivalent inductance of the coil calculated so that the thickness of the air gap may be determined experimentally to check with the calculated results. The dynamic B-H curve is a part of the hysteresis loop and examples are given. Formulas for the magnetic loss and the principle of measurement on this circuit are then discussed.

articleTitle: Non-Volatile Station Memory Single Chip Including Remote-Control Receiver and Memory-Display Driver
abstract: A new single chip designed for TV digital-tuning applications is presented. Besides integrating all the functions required for a complete non-volatile memory voltage synthesis tuning system, the chip includes complete PCM I.R. remote control receiver and direct memory-display driving section. Details of the main features are presented.

articleTitle: A High Resolution Bar Code Reader
abstract: For a long time a need has existed for an inexpensive, highly reliable, optical "wand" with extremely fine resolution, to provide the capability of very dense bar code reading. This need has been fulfilled through the development of a wand that was initially used in conjunction with a speaking learning aid. To date, approximately 100,000 of these wands have been manufactured and used with the initially intended learning aid, but uses with other existing products, and with future products are already planned.

articleTitle: Recording and Playing (R/P) System Having a Compatibility with Mass Produced Replica Disc
abstract: It has now been several years since the first laser video disc system made its debut on the market and the years since then have seen the development of many new applications utilizing various features of the system. The most outstanding features of the laser video disc system are high recording density, high speed of information retrieval, and high speed of copying of information.

articleTitle: Triple Color Signal Process IC for VCR
abstract: Recently the home video Cassette Recorder (VCR) has remarkably come into world-wide use. However, complicating the situation are three different kinds of television standards: NTSC, PAL and SECAM, and the specifications of their chrominance signal are different from each other.

articleTitle: Transmission of Musical Information in a Teletext Multiplexed Broadcasting System
abstract: Nippon Television Network Inc. has been experimenting since December of 1981 on a code method teletext multiplexed broadcasting system. To have a significantly large number of viewers watch teletext broadcasts on a daily basis, broad ranging, pertinent and visually interesting information must be provided. To achieve this, more is required than the conventional combinations of characters and mosaics, and in addition to these, detailed graphics and musical accompaniment are highly desirable. Therefore, Nippon Television Network's experiments focus chiefly on compressed transmission of detailed graphics information and the transmission of musical information by means of note encoding. In the following we wish to present an overview of the musical transmission system currently under experiment. In Japan, experiments on a standardized system for code method teletext have been underway, and musical information transmission system reported on here is being adopted as a standard.

articleTitle: Battery Systems for Electronic Devices
Automatic Misregistration Testing Apparatus for Line Screen Color CRT'S
abstract: Optimum color CRT performance requires that the electron beam impinge on the screen at the proper phosphor stripe. The extent to which the beam fails to strike the intended phosphor stripe is referred to as misregistration. Misregistration leads to loss of purity and luminance. Among the many factors which influence the extent of misregistration, perhaps the most important is the quality of the exposure lens used in the process to deposit the phosphor stripes on the screen. Exposure lens development is quite labor-intensive and is subject to human error.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of the Power Dividers with Ferrite Toroids for CATV and/or MATV Systems
abstract: The frequency characteristics for the power dividers with ferrite toroids, which are extensively used in CATV and/or MATV systems, are analyzed. The analytical optimum design method for the weakly-coupled power divider by the simplified model and the numerical optimum design method for the tightly-coupled power divider by the exact model are proposed, and the designed power dividers with ferrite toroids by the proposed methods have much improved frequency characteristics compared with the original power dividers. Thus, the useful bandwiths of all the power dividers have been extended from 5 to 500 MHz. Practical measurements show very good agreements with theoretical results, and, hence, the validity of the analyses and design methods for the power dividers with ferrite toroids are confirmed. Furthermore, the relations between the optimum circuit and ferrite constants have been clarified in reference to L0(i)Kfm.

articleTitle: Homenet: A Control Network for Consumer Applications
abstract: Homenet fills the need for a low cost network for the exchange of control information among a broad spectrum of consumer applications in the home. Just as cablevision and telephone media are stimulating delivery of new services the home, Homenet's purpose is to provide a standardized control network within the home for innovative consumer products and to complement these and other external delivery systems. Homenet is designed to handle applications ranging from rudimentary functions like on-off remote controls to complex non-data-intensive functions like energy management, security, entertainment module coordination, and clock synchronization.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Analog/Digital Proportional Control System for Home Computer and Robotics Applications
abstract: This paper describes an integrated circuit chip set* designed for low-cost transmission of analog and digital data. The system provides remote motion control capability and is designed for home computer or microprocessor control applications. The control system is based on a multichannel serial bus concept and uses pulse-position modulation (PPM) for information transfer. The input and output of the system interface directly with a home or personal computer.

articleTitle: Indoor Unit for Direct Broadcast Satellite (DBS) (RF to Demodulation Part)
abstract: The suggested specifications of WARC 77 represent a reliable and stable reference upon which the work of DBS receiver designers must be based (1).

articleTitle: A Vocal Editor
abstract: Although the speech quality produced by the currently available speech synthesizers is far from high fidelity standard, it is possible using a similar approach to produce high-quality vocals. To achieve this, the imperfection of the automatic analysis must be manually corrected. Such operations are already done for speech synthesis, but for vocals the operations required are significantly different.
